brief: The Market Ear's September 10 call that bond vol was underpriced has been validated: rates had been rising in an orderly fashion, but yesterday the 10-year surged and MOVE spiked, which the note reads as the orderly phase ending. The 10-year is up roughly 25bps over two weeks and 35bps over the past month, approaching the threshold GS flags for when equities start reacting to rate moves (a 2-sigma move, about 30bps in two weeks or 50bps in a month). The core argument: for equities, the speed of the rates move matters more than the yield level itself, and SPX has so far held up even as the 10-year and MOVE have broken sharply, widening the gap between stocks and rates. Technically, yesterday's surge pushed the 10-year to levels last seen roughly two decades ago; after three years of consolidation the breakout opens a vacuum above the range, with 5.2% the first level to watch and 5.5% beyond that.
